definition: An impromptu public speech delivered in Shelf markets, transit hubs, or under-bridge encampments — typically political, anti-corponation, or synth-rights focused. Some are genuine agitation; many are performance for Diaspora bleed feeds. Ferrogate Security classifies them as 'pre-riot indicators.'
origin: Shelf street culture, blending religious oratory tradition with scrap-pile aesthetics of Shelf public spaces
usage: Shelf agitators, synth-rights activists, underworld recruiters, Diaspora journalists
example: The scrap sermon drew forty people under the Overhang before Ferrogate showed up — by then the speaker was already three tunnels gone.
